column1: # Where each gloss in lex-de.tsv was read.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quote | stands
# The gloss is the English word a German word is woven for, and the tooltip
# prints it back: it is the claim every reader meets first. Every other
# claim the pack makes about a word names its entry — genders in
# de-genders.tsv, plurals in de-plurals.tsv, verb forms in de-verb-forms.tsv
# — and the gloss named none until 2026-10-08, the night fr-, es- and
# pt-glosses.tsv were written the same way.
# Every row is read, all 356: the 178 nouns, 81 verbs, 57 adjectives, 22
# adverbs, 13 numerals and 5 interjections. Each was read in the rendered
# page of the word's English Wiktionary entry, in its German section: a
# script took the definition lines under each heading of the row's part of
# speech, examples, quotations and synonyms set aside, and drafted the first
# that holds the row's English word, and every quote was read against its
# page. Three drafts were another sense, and their lines quote the row's:
# Schild's page holds two nouns, das Schild, a sign, whose third line is a
# "(nonstandard or informal …) alternative form of Schild", and der Schild,
# "shield, buckler", the seed's masculine; haben's first line is the
# auxiliary; and suchen's line holding "seek" is its formal sense, "to seek,
# to strive, to intend, to try", where the row's is "to search, to look for".
# German titles keep their capitals, and the disk the pages were read from
# does not: Essen.html and essen.html are one file there, so Essen, food,
# first read as the verb essen, arm, poor, as the noun Arm, and leben and
# morgen as Leben and Morgen. Each was read again from its own page before
# A page holds every word of one spelling, so a quote is from this word's
# own part of speech where the page has it. Two rows' words have none of
# theirs, and their lines quote the heading the page gives them: erste,
# "first", is an ordinal adjective, and bitte, "please", gives the word as
# an adverb, its interjections being "you're welcome", "excuse me" and
# The title is the word as Wiktionary's address writes it, capitals kept and
# an underscore for a space: wikt:de:auf_Wiedersehen. A noun cites the entry
# its gender was read in, which for every German noun is its own.
# Blank where the quote holds the row's English word. Otherwise it names the
# word of the quote that stands for it, because the English word is not in
# the entry, or is there only in another sense. Two rows need one: suchen
# for "seek" is "to search, to look for", and wirklich for "truly" "really,
# None is false. One says less than the row is woven for, and is recorded
# rather than changed: erinnern alone is "(transitive) to remind", and
# "remember" is its reflexive's, "to remember, to be reminded of", as French
# tests/tools/glosses.test.ts requires every row of lex-de.tsv to have a line
# here citing its own word's entry, whose quote holds its English word or the
# stand-in it names, and fails on a line outliving its row.
